notes: Exact normalized subject-name matches with the same departmental flag are reused verbatim even if syllabus descriptions differ, per user instruction.

For non-name matches, reuse still requires departmental-flag and unit/topic alignment. An exact-name match with an incompatible departmental flag raises an error rather than silently generating a replacement bank.
Mid 1 scope is recorded from the first half of the ordered syllabus units; confirm against the official exam blueprint.
Generated question pools and theory answers are drafts requiring academic review.
TestsData contains only TestId, Questions, Options and Answers; mappings are held in test_index.
Theory rows use Options=[] and model answers in Answers; consumers must explicitly support both formats.
Project subjects excluded entirely; no TestIds created.
Generated items require academic QA before use.

subjects.name: Advance Java
subjects.objective: This course develops programming ability of students to create dynamic web applications using server side technology with Java Database Connectivity. Students can learn networking and remote method invocation using Java API. Different Java frameworks like Spring, Java Server Faces and Hibernate will increase ability of students in web application development. Credits Earned: 4 Credits
course_outcomes: After completion of this course, student will be able to ● Describe the components of J2EE Architecture, MVC Framework and Multi-tier ● Application and Various Network Protocol. (Remember) ● To make use of Servlet and JSP API in the process of enterprise application deployment. (Understand) ● Implement components such as Session, Filters, JSTL, Beans. (Apply) ● Distinguish Application Server, Web Container, JDBC and ORM tools.(Analyze) ● Design and Development of web application having collaboration of Servlets, JSPs, JSF, Spring and Hibernate base upon the requirement. (Apply).

allSyllabusUnits.title: JDBC Programming
allSyllabusUnits.topics: JDBC connectivity model, connecting to databases, creating SQL queries, retrieving query results, updating database data, error checking, SQLException, SQLWarning, Statement interface, PreparedStatement, CallableStatement, ResultSet interface, updatable ResultSets, JDBC types

allSyllabusUnits.title: J2EE Architecture, Servlets and JSP
allSyllabusUnits.topics: J2EE architecture, multi tier applications, MVC framework, network protocols, Servlet API, JSP API, web containers, application deployment

allSyllabusUnits.title: Enterprise Web Components
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Sessions, filters, JSTL, JavaBeans, servlet processing, JSP pages, web application state management

allSyllabusUnits.title: Java Networking and Remote Method Invocation
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Java networking, network protocols, remote method invocation RMI, client server communication

allSyllabusUnits.title: Java Web Frameworks and ORM
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Java Server Faces JSF, Spring framework, Hibernate, JDBC, object relational mapping ORM tools, dynamic web applications

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: JDBC Programming; J2EE Architecture, Servlets and JSP; Enterprise Web Components.

subjects.name: Big Data Analytics
subjects.objective: Big data is an extremely useful area in the era of computing techniques as it aids in finding useful patterns from large datasets. Large datasets are so huge that they cannot be processed with traditional technologies. We require a special computing system which can handle large data and tandem it with other important aspects like parallel processing, data failure and data pre-processing.
course_outcomes: After completion of this course, student will be able to and its Tools. (Understand) • Gain Understanding about Big Data Technology • Understand and apply extracting useful patterns from large datasets.industry.(Analyze)(Apply) • Implementation of Big data mining techniques using different software. (Create) •(Apply)Understand how data analytics and data science maps to current • Understanding and implementing Algorithms in an optimized way using various Big Data Tools. Prerequisite of course: Basic knowledge of C language

allSyllabusUnits.title: Big Data and Hadoop Foundations
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Traditional distributed file systems, Big Data software, Big Data applications, Hadoop architecture, how Hadoop works, Hadoop ecosystem, basic Hadoop commands, HDFS

allSyllabusUnits.title: MapReduce and Hadoop Ecosystem Tools
allSyllabusUnits.topics: MapReduce programming, input formats, output formats, key value pairs, Pig Latin structures, Pig statements, Pig functions, loading and storing data in Pig, HiveQL, Hive tables, HBase, ZooKeeper services

allSyllabusUnits.title: Apache Spark and Distributed Analytics
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Apache Spark, PySpark, Resilient Distributed Datasets RDD, key value pairs, loading data, saving data, Spark machine learning library, distributed data analytics

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Big Data and Hadoop Foundations; MapReduce and Hadoop Ecosystem Tools.

subjects.name: Cloud Computing
subjects.objective: This course is intended to analyse the basics of cloud computing, and make aware students with diversified technologies working for cloud architecture. Course will be focusing on architecture, service models, privacy & security in the cloud. Credits Earned: 5 Credits
course_outcomes: After learning this course, students should be able to, 1. Understand and analyse the architecture of Cloud (Analyse). 2. Identify and apply deployment and management options of AWS Cloud Architecture (Apply). 3. Design architectures to decouple infrastructure and reduce interdependencies (Create). 4. Monitor Cloud-Based Resources, creating dashboards, Creating Alarms and configuring notification alerts (Create).

firstHalfUnits.title: Introduction of Cloud & Amazon Web Service

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction of Cloud & Amazon Web Service
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction of cloud computing, What is Virtualization , Infrastructure as a Service(IaaS), Software as a Service(Saas), Platform as a Service(PaaS), Advantages of Cloud, AWS history , Dashboard, AWS Overview, Architecture Discussion Marwadi University Faculty of Diploma studies Information and Communication Technology

allSyllabusUnits.title: Identity & Access Management
allSyllabusUnits.topics: IAM Overview and Policies, IAM Users, Groups, Access Key & Secret Access Key, MFA, Report

allSyllabusUnits.title: Elastic Cloud Computing (EC2)
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Amazon EC2 Overview, Elastic Block Storage(EBS), Amazon Machine Image(AMI), Introduction to EC2 Instance Types, Security Group, Public & private IP Overview, Amazon EBS & Snapshot, AWS CLI

allSyllabusUnits.title: Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3)
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Simple Storage Service (S3), S3 Object Storage and Buckets, Web Hosting , Glacier, Versioning

allSyllabusUnits.title: Cloud Watch Monitoring & SNS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Monitor Cloud-Based Resources, creating dashboards, Creating Alarms and configuring notification alerts

allSyllabusUnits.title: Route 53 & Databases
allSyllabusUnits.topics: DNS Records, Website Hosting, Relational Database System, DB engine & Instance details, Setup and Connect MySQL database Total 42 hrs.

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Introduction of Cloud & Amazon Web Service; Identity & Access Management; Elastic Cloud Computing (EC2).

subjects.name: Computer Graphics & Animation
subjects.objective: This course facilitates classroom and laboratory learning, letting students learn concepts of graphics and animation. Students will learn different algorithms of graphics and types of transformations. Students will understand 2D and 3Dmodels and operations on it. Student will also learn about creating animations. Credits Earned: 04 Credits
course_outcomes: After completion of this course, student will be able to: 1. Understand basic concepts, tools and algorithms of computer graphics (Understand) 2. Use matrix algebra in computer graphics applications. (Apply) 3. Implement fundamental algorithms and transformations involved in viewing models, projection models, illumination models and the handling of hidden surfaces in polygon-based computer graphics. (Apply) 4. Create Animation by applying fundamentals of animation and digital image processing.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Overview of computer graphics, computer graphics applications, graphics software, graphics devices, input devices, active and passive graphics devices, display technologies, storage tube displays, calligraphic refresh displays, raster refresh displays, CRT basics, color CRT raster scan, video controller, LCD displays

allSyllabusUnits.title: Scan Conversion and Clipping
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Digital Differential Analyzer DDA line drawing, Bresenham line drawing, Bresenham circle drawing, midpoint circle algorithm, midpoint ellipse algorithm, aliasing, endpoint ordering, Cohen Sutherland clipping, Cyrus Beck clipping, Liang Barsky clipping, polygon clipping

allSyllabusUnits.title: 2D and 3D Transformations, Viewing and Rendering
allSyllabusUnits.topics: 2D transformations, transformation matrices, homogeneous coordinates, translation, rotation, reflection, scaling, combined transformations, 3D scaling, shearing, rotation, reflection, translation, perspective transformations, orthographic projections, axonometric projections, oblique projections, 3D viewing, lighting, color, z buffer, scan line, painter's algorithm, BSP trees, ray tracing

allSyllabusUnits.title: Curves and Surfaces
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Curve representation, non parametric curves, parametric curves, circle representation, ellipse representation, parabola representation, hyperbola representation, space curves, cubic splines, Bezier curves, B spline curves, quadric surfaces, Bezier surfaces

allSyllabusUnits.title: Computer Animation and Image Processing
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Principles of animation, key framing, deformations, character animation, physics based animation, procedural techniques, groups of objects, digital image formats, JPEG compression, image enhancement, contrast stretching, histogram equalization, smoothing filters, median filtering

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Introduction to Computer Graphics; Scan Conversion and Clipping; 2D and 3D Transformations, Viewing and Rendering.

subjects.name: Cyber Security
subjects.objective: Cryptography is an indispensable tool for protecting information in computer systems. It deals with the algorithmic and mathematical perspective of information and network security. In this course you will learn the inner workings of cryptographic systems and how to correctly use them in real-world applications. Credits Earned: 04 Credits
course_outcomes: After the completion of the course, the students will be able to: 1. To categorize common types of security threats are risks to the Computer Systems and the nature of common Information hazards. 2. Identify the potential threats to confidentiality, integrity and availability of Computer Systems at personal and organizational level. 3. Gain understanding of different requirements and principles for Electronic Mail, IP Security and Web Security with monitoring and analysis of networks. 4. Gain the understanding and requirements of different firewalls and other wireless security standards.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction and Security Threats
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Threats to security: Viruses and Worms, Intruders, Insiders, Criminal organizations, Terrorists, Information warfare Avenues of Attack, steps in attack, Security Basics –Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability Types of attack: Denial of service (DOS), backdoors and trapdoors, sniffing, spoofing, man in the middle, replay, TCP/IP Hacking, Phishing attacks, Distributed DOS, SQL Injection. Malware: Viruses, Logic bombs

allSyllabusUnits.title: Organizational Security
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Password selection, Piggybacking, Shoulder surfing, Dumpster diving, Installing unauthorized software, hardware, Access by non- employees. People as Security Tool: Security awareness, and Individual user responsibilities. Physical security: Access controls Biometrics: finger prints, hand prints, Retina, Patterns, voice patterns, signature and writing patterns, keystrokes, Physical barriers

allSyllabusUnits.title: IP Security
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Overview of IP Security (IPSec); IP Security Architecture; Modes of Operation; Security Associations (SA) Security Parameter Index (SPI), SA Management, Security Policy; Authentication Header (AH); Internet Key Exchange –

allSyllabusUnits.title: Web Security
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Web Security Requirements; Secure Socket Layer (SSL) SSL Architecture, SSL Protocol; Transport Layer Security (TLS); Secure Electronic Transaction (SET) Features, Components, Dual Signature,– Purchase Request.5 Electronic Mail Security: – 8 Threats to E-Mail; Requirements and Solutions Confidentiality, Integrity; Encryption for Secure E-Mail; Secure E-Mail System PGP (Pretty Good Privacy), S/MIME (Secure Multipurpose Internet– Mail Extensions).6 Firewalls: – 4 Firewalls, Types, Packet Filtering Gateway, Stateful Inspection Firewall, Application Proxy, Guard, Personal Firewalls

allSyllabusUnits.title: Wireless Network Security Standards
allSyllabusUnits.topics: IEEE 802.11, IEEE 802.11i Wireless LAN Security, WAP protocol, WAP End-to-End Security Total 43 hrs

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Introduction and Security Threats; Organizational Security; IP Security.

subjects.name: Embedded Systems
subjects.objective: The objective of the subject is to introduce the concepts of embedded systems and AVR microcontroller architecture, programming and various applications based on it. Credits Earned: 4
course_outcomes: After learning this course, students should be able to, 1. Learn the concepts of embedded system 2. Understand the features of AVR microcontroller 3. Apply programming skill to interface necessary hardware with microcontroller 4. Develop AVR microcontroller based systems

firstHalfUnits.title: AVR Microcontroller Architecture and assembly language

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction to Embedded Systems
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Embedded Systems, Processor Embedded into a System, Embedded Hardware Units and Devices In a System, Embedded Software in a system, Examples of Embedded Systems, Embedded System-on-chip (SOC) and Use of VLSI Circuit Design Technology, Complex Systems Design and Processors, Design Process in Embedded System, Formulization of System Design, Design Process and Design Examples, Classification of Embedded Systems, Skills Required for an Embedded System Designer

allSyllabusUnits.title: AVR microcontroller-History and Features
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Microcontrollers and embedded processors, Criteria for choosing a microcontroller, Simplified view of AVR microcontroller, ATMega32 block diagram, Overview of AVR family Marwadi University Faculty of Diploma studies Information and Communication Technology

allSyllabusUnits.title: AVR Microcontroller Architecture and assembly language
allSyllabusUnits.topics: programming: General Purpose registers in AVR, The AVR data memory, AVR status register, AVR data formats and assembler directives, Assembly Language Programming, Program Counter and program ROM space in AVR, RISC architecture in AVR, Branch Instructions, CALL instruction and Stack, Pipelining, Time delay loop , AVR I/O port programming, Arithmetic and Logic instructions, AVR advanced assembly language programming, Bit addressability, MACROs, Intel HEX file, AVR Hardware pin connections

allSyllabusUnits.title: AVR programming in C
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Data types and time delay in C, I/O port programming in C, Logic operations in C, Data conversion programs in C, Data serialization in C, Memory allocation in C, AVR Timer programming in C, AVR interrupt programming in C, AVR serial port programming in C

allSyllabusUnits.title: AVR Interfacing
allSyllabusUnits.topics: LCD and Keyboard Interfacing, Relay and optoisolator interfacing, Stepper and DC Motor control, ADC,DAC and sensor interfacing, SPI Protocol and MAX7221 display interfacing, I2C Protocol and DS1307 RTC Interfacing Total 42 hrs.

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Introduction to Embedded Systems; AVR microcontroller-History and Features; AVR Microcontroller Architecture and assembly language.

subjects.name: Fundamental of Data Mining
subjects.objective: This course focuses on both concepts and practice. We will introduce (a) the core data mining concepts and practical skills for applying data mining techniques to solve real-world problems. Credits Earned: 04
course_outcomes: After completion of this course, student will be able to: 1. Understand about Data mining, Clustering and Data processing. 2. Describe the Data mining Tool and its various techniques. 3. Interpret the various Clustering methods and Data mining Application. 4. Evaluate different data mining techniques like classification, prediction, clustering and association rule mining. 5. Apply appropriate data mining algorithms to solve real world problems

allSyllabusUnits.title: Data Mining and Data Processing
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Data mining concepts, data processing, data preprocessing, data processing systems, data preparation, data quality, data mining tools

allSyllabusUnits.title: Data Mining Techniques
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Association rules, classification, regression, clustering, neural networks, predictive modeling, mining technique selection

allSyllabusUnits.title: Clustering Methods
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Cluster analysis, K means clustering, hierarchical clustering, agglomerative clustering, divisive clustering, cluster evaluation, segmentation software

allSyllabusUnits.title: Applications of Data Mining
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Data mining applications, business applications, risk management, targeted marketing, customer profiles, prediction, evaluating data mining results

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Data Mining and Data Processing; Data Mining Techniques.

subjects.name: Management Information System
subjects.objective: The main goals of a MIS are to help executives of an organization make decisions that advance the organization’s strategy and to implement the organizational structure and dynamics of the enterprise for the purpose of managing the organization in a better way for a competitive advantage. Credits Earned: 02 Credits
course_outcomes: After completion of this course, student will be able to: 1. Understand need and importance of Management Information System. [Remember] 2. Elaborate the supporting role of Management in decision-making. [Analyze] 3. Interpret the role of MIS in various functional areas of management. [Understand] 4. Develop and integration of information with MIS.[Apply]

firstHalfUnits.title: Decision Support Systems and Business Intelligence

allSyllabusUnits.title: Information Systems and MIS Fundamentals
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Information systems and their roles, classify information, management information systems, benefits of MIS, limitations of MIS

allSyllabusUnits.title: MIS Development and Design
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Systems analysts, tools used by system analysts, MIS development life cycle, MIS development models, MIS design

allSyllabusUnits.title: Decision Support Systems and Business Intelligence
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Decision support systems DSS, management and decision making, types of decisions, analytics, business intelligence, BI techniques

allSyllabusUnits.title: Managing the IT Function
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Challenges of managing IT functions, modern IT environment, centralization, decentralization, IT security, technology selection, vendor management, vendor selection, vendor contracts, service levels, relationship management

allSyllabusUnits.title: Integration of Information Systems
allSyllabusUnits.topics: MIS integration with business functions, enterprise resource planning ERP, business process outsourcing BPO, electronic commerce

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Information Systems and MIS Fundamentals; MIS Development and Design; Decision Support Systems and Business Intelligence.

subjects.name: RF and Microwave Communication
subjects.objective: The rationale behind this course is to understand RF and Microwave systems. Credits Earned: 4 Credits
course_outcomes: After learning this course, students should be able to, 1. Understand basic concepts and applications of microwave systems. 2. Analyze and solve problems related to microwave transmission lines. 3. Analyze and solve problems related to microwave waveguides. 4. Learn to apply use of various passive and active microwave components for different applications. 5. Understand working of microwave amplifier, oscillator, and mixer circuits.

firstHalfUnits.title: Analysis of Microwave Transmission Lines and Waveguides

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction to Microwaves
allSyllabusUnits.topics: History of Microwaves, Microwave frequency bands, General applications of Microwaves, Advantages of Microwaves, Microwave Propagation

allSyllabusUnits.title: Mathematical model of Microwave Transmission
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Concept of Mode, Characteristics of TEM, TE and TM Modes, Losses associated with microwave transmission, Concept of Impedance in Microwave transmission Marwadi University Faculty of Diploma studies Information and Communication Technology

allSyllabusUnits.title: Analysis of Microwave Transmission Lines and Waveguides
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Transmission line equations & solutions, reflection and transmission coefficient, standing wave and standing wave ratio, line impedance and admittance, impedance matching, using stub line, skin effect, application of smith chart in solving transmission line problems, Introduction to strip lines, Micro strip lines, Rectangular and circular waveguides

allSyllabusUnits.title: Microwave Network Analysis
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Equivalent voltages and currents for non-TEM lines, Network parameters for microwave circuits, Scattering Parameters

allSyllabusUnits.title: Passive and Active RF and microwave Devices
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Microwave Passive components: Directional Coupler, Power Divider, Magic Tee, Hybrid ring, Wave-guide Corners, Bends, Twists, Attenuator, Circulator, Isolator and Resonator. Microwave Active components: Tunnel diode, Varactor diodes, Step recovery diodes, Schottky Barrier diodes, PIN diodes, Gunn Diodes, IMPATT and TRAPATT diodes, Parametric Amplifiers, Microwave Transistors, Microwave oscillators and Mixers, Klystron, Magnetron

allSyllabusUnits.title: Microwave Frequency Measurement: Wavelength, VSWR,
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Attenuation and Microwave Radiation Hazards: type and protection from hazards Total ‘Q’, 42 hrs.

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Introduction to Microwaves; Mathematical model of Microwave Transmission; Analysis of Microwave Transmission Lines and Waveguides.

subjects.name: Sensor and IoT (SIoT)
subjects.objective: The rationale behind this course is to learn to understand working of sensor, sensor interfacing and develop IoT solutions. Credits Earned: 4 Credits
course_outcomes: After learning this course, students should be able to, CO1: To understand the concept of IoT and its architecture. CO2: Interfacing of various sensors with programmable boards CO3: To write programs for various IoT applications. CO4: Integration of various sensors and data transfer protocols. CO5: To develop solutions for different topics in society by means of IoT.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction to Internet of Things
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Definitions, core concepts, related concepts, IoT reference models, IoT architectures, challenges, IoT functional stack

allSyllabusUnits.title: Sensors
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Working principles, different types, selection of sensors for practical applications, Introduction to different types of sensors such as capacitive, resistive, temperature, humidity, pressure, ultrasonic, gas, Hall effect, PIR, MEMS, Image, IR, Proximity, GPS and GSM module, Interfacing sensor with IoT hardware boards Marwadi University Faculty of Diploma studies Information and Communication Technology

allSyllabusUnits.title: Communication devices and protocols
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Bluetooth and BLE, Wifi, Zigbee, IPv6, 6LowPAN, LTE-M, RFID, NFC, LiDAR

allSyllabusUnits.title: Application layer: MQTT, CoAP, XMPP, Integrating internet services
allSyllabusUnits.topics: with interoperable data encoding with XML, JSON, CBOR, sensor markup language, lightweight web services for IoT

allSyllabusUnits.title: IoT application domains: Smart Cities, Smart Manufacturing, Smart Grid,
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Smart Buildings, Intelligent Transportation Systems, Healthcare Total 42 hrs.

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Introduction to Internet of Things; Sensors; Communication devices and protocols.

subjects.name: Wireless Technologies
subjects.objective: This course is to make students learn about fundamentals of wireless technologies and various wireless networking architectures. They will also go through significantly latest wireless technologies. Credits Earned: 4 Credits
course_outcomes: After learning this course, students should be able to, 1. Understand basic concepts of cellular communication systems. 2. Understand about basic principles behind radio resource management techniques such as power control, channel allocation and handoffs. 3. Evaluate different wireless communication systems and standards. 4. Compare different technologies used for wireless communication systems. 5. Explain the architecture, functioning, protocols, capabilities and application of various wireless communication systems.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction to Cellular Communication
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Cellular cell concepts: cell structure, frequency reuse, cell splitting, cell sectoring, Microcell zone concept, channel assignment, interference, capacity, power control, Evolution of cellular communication systems: overview and standards of 1G, 2G, 3G and 4G systems Marwadi University Faculty of Diploma studies Information and Communication Technology

allSyllabusUnits.title: Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM)
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Services and Features, System Architecture, Radio sub systems, Channel types, Example of a GSM call, Frame Structure, Signal Processing, Protocols, Hand off, GPRS: Architecture, Protocols and Channels, security

allSyllabusUnits.title: CDMA
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Architecture of IS-95 CDMA system, CDMA forward channels, CDMA reverse channels, Soft handoff, CDMA features, Power control in CDMA, Performance of CDMA System, RAKE Receiver, CDMA2000 cellular technology

allSyllabusUnits.title: Wireless Personal Area Networks: Bluetooth Specifications, Protocols
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Stack, Security Issues, Advantages and Disadvantages, Application, UWB, Zigbee, wireless local area networks: IEEE 802.11, network architecture, medium access methods, WLAN standards, wireless metropolitan area networks: Wimax

allSyllabusUnits.title: GPS, wireless local loop, cordless phone, paging systems, RFID, Home RF,
allSyllabusUnits.topics: NFC, Software Defined Radio, Wireless Sensor Networks, Security issues and challenges in wireless networks Total 42 hrs.

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Introduction to Cellular Communication; Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM); CDMA.
